scenarios.name: Cloud Object Storage Implementation Controls
scenarios.problem_scenario: Does the architecture implement upload, storage, and download through cloud object storage?
risk_identification: Objects may be exposed through public bucket policy or weak ACL configuration.
Uploaded malicious content may be distributed through signed download links.
security_control_requirements: Enforce private bucket policy and block public access.
Generate short-lived signed URLs server-side only.
Validate object metadata, MIME type, and file magic number.
Scan uploaded objects before releasing download links.
verification_points: API design defines signed URL expiration.
Implementation plan includes malware scanning and type validation.

scenarios.name: Cloud IAM Least Privilege
scenarios.problem_scenario: Does the design use cloud IAM roles, API keys, or service principals for cloud resource access?
risk_identification: Over-privileged cloud identity may allow unauthorized resource modification.
Static keys may be leaked through logs, CI/CD variables, or configuration files.
security_control_requirements: Use least-privilege IAM roles with scoped permissions.
Prefer short-lived credentials over static keys.
Store secrets in a managed secret store and never in repository files.
Enable audit logging for cloud API usage.
verification_points: IAM permissions are documented per resource.
No static cloud keys are stored in config files.
Audit logging and credential rotation are included in the implementation plan.
